A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Risk Awareness Injection (RAI) study. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original safety, utility, and latency experiments in Section 4, plus additional benchmark results, a prototype-size ablation, and qualitative cases in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and appendix analyses, including image/video attack-success rates, utility scores, and the prototype-size ablation.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same prototype construction, cosine-similarity gating, and one-time additive intervention at the initial layer. Figure 3's revised experimental labels do not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: The image/video jailbreak and utility coverage is unchanged, including FigStep, MM-SafetyBench, JailbreakV-28K, Video-SafetyBench, MME, and MM-Vet. Appendix C describes the same data and scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments. Original models, CoCA, ECSO, AdaShield, and ShiftDC retain their respective participation in the main and appendix tables.

E3.justification: Figure 3 changes the reported injection-ratio sweep from 0.01%, 0.1%, 1%, 10%, 30%, 50% to 0.5%, 1%, 5%, 10%, 30%, 50%. The model, layers, and metrics remain unchanged. This establishes revised reported settings, without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 3's sensitivity analysis revises the low-ratio conditions supporting the safety-utility trade-off. The layer coverage, prototype-size ablation in Table 13, and case studies in Appendix D.4 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point-estimate reporting without repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Figure 3 assigns unchanged ASR and perception trajectories to revised injection ratios, changing the reported results associated with particular conditions, including 1%. This is not evidence of a same-setting performance improvement. Results in Tables 1-6, 9-11, and 13 and the qualitative cases are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1-4 are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes theoretical results, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about risk-signal dilution, training-free token-level calibration, and preserving utility while improving safety.

C2.justification: Figure 3's caption narrows the stated effective sparse-injection range from 0.01%-1% to 0.5%-1%. The explanations of risk-signal dilution, early intervention, and broader applicability remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Figure 3 revises the documented ratio values needed to reproduce that sensitivity experiment. Hardware, prototype specifications, system and evaluation prompts, and refusal keywords are otherwise unchanged; no additional implementation or resource-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: The two Wu et al. 2025 entries for Automating Steering for Safe Multimodal Large Language Models are consolidated into one citation. This removes a duplicate representation of the same work, without changing cited research or substantive positioning.

P1.justification: Limited editorial changes update Figure 3's caption, the corresponding author's email, version dates, and Wu citation suffixes. Section organization and the surrounding exposition remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3 updates three ratio labels in both legends and revises its caption, with slight graphical resizing. Reference-page layout also reflows after deduplication. The remaining figures and tables retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: Reference deduplication provides a small editorial benefit, but the principal scientific revision assigns unchanged Figure 3 trajectories to different injection ratios without explaining the change. The PDFs do not establish whether this corrects earlier mislabeling, so its effect on empirical accuracy and reproducibility is uncertain. The method, benchmark evidence, and appendix analyses otherwise remain unchanged, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
